key_insight: EP-Flow predicts disordered crystal structures from chemical formulas by modeling site occupancies as a constrained occupancy distribution matrix instead of requiring site-level disorder labels.
engineering_relevance: This enables practical inverse design of real materials with disorder, such as solid solutions, vacancy-rich phases, and interstitially occupied compounds, where disorder strongly affects performance.
method: Represents disorder with an Occupancy Distribution Matrix (ODM) over sites and species.
Uses Entropic Polytope Flow to map formula-dependent feasible occupancy polytopes into a shared double-centered space.
Recovers physically valid occupancies with a Sinkhorn inverse map while co-generating coordinates and lattice parameters.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports state-of-the-art results on formula-conditioned disordered crystal structure prediction benchmarks built from COD and MPDS, outperforming adapted ordered-crystal generators.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurately enforcing marginal and feasibility constraints, so numerical stability and Sinkhorn convergence may be important implementation bottlenecks.
paper_title: EP-Flow: Disordered Crystal Structure Prediction without Site-Level Annotations
